The Invisibility of Value

Value has no physical existence. It cannot express itself in isolation. A commodity can
only reveal its value by entering into a social relationship with a different commodity.

Price: The Ideal Money-Form
Price is merely the "money-name" of the labor realized in a commodity. Because
expressing value in gold is a purely mental act, it requires only imaginary money.
The commodity's value lives in its owner's head until it hits the market.

sold to realize that value. If the market is saturated or the labor was not
socially necessary, the leap falls short, and the value is lost.

The seller exchanges a commodity for money, only to exchange that money for a different commodity.

The Velocity of Currency
Commodities: Linear & Finite (Falling into Consumption)
Money: Continuous & Infinite (Perpetually Replacing Goods)
Commodities fall out of circulation once purchased. Money, however, is continuously precipitated into
the space vacated by the commodity. This creates the optical illusion that money is circulating the
commodities, rather than the commodities circulating the money.

The Secret of the Commodity
A commodity appears trivial at first glance. But once an object steps forth as a commodity,
it is changed into something transcendent. It stands on its head and evolves grotesque,
mystical ideas. Whence arises this enigmatical character?
